whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim in California, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your options.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Perfect
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In an ordinary injury case, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your compensation isn't artificially limited by a statutory ceiling.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money. There's no retainer and no hourly bill to worry about.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in California?
items.answer: Most personal injury claims have a two-year statute of limitations from the date of the incident. If your claim involves a government entity or agency, the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Imperial?
items.answer: Based on public collision records, corridors such as Rt 86, Aten Road, 2nd Street, and Clark Road show up frequently in reported crash counts, and Friday afternoons between noon and 2 p.m. see more reports than other times. These are simply patterns in public data, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney. We are not a law firm, and there's no cost to you for using our connection service.

items.question: How much can I expect to recover?
items.answer: There's no way to predict an outcome or dollar amount, since every case depends on its own facts and evidence. An independent attorney can review the details of what happened and talk through what might be possible in your situation.
